Team —

Quick status: we ingested the traces and started correlating with infra metrics. Early signal: a small subset of our hosted GPU nodes are showing sustained allocator fragmentation on the device heap (we're seeing growing slab-unusable segments and repeated device OOMs followed by driver-level recovery that stalls the runtime). That pattern produces rare but very expensive stalls on token generation — which matches the p99-only nature of the spike.

Immediate mitigations applied (17:05 PT):
- Removed ~8 nodes from the Veritas serving pool to route traffic away from affected instances.
- Forced a small rolling restart of the GPU worker group with a patch to increase slab coalescing window (runtime-side flag).
- Disabled aggressive KV-prefetch for Veritas model variant to reduce prefetch churn.

Observed effect: p99 reduced from 2.4s to ~600ms within 12 minutes; 500s errors dropped to near zero. Still monitoring.

Monica
Sr. SRE, Runtime Operations
Redwood Inference

Follow-up from runtime diagnostics:

Root cause hypothesis: an allocator slab-growth interaction with our kernel selection path caused persistent fragmentation under certain long-sequence workloads. That is, when large KV-cache windows and intermittent long-sequence requests coincide, the allocator doesn't reclaim contiguous device blocks efficiently. Over ~48–72 hours this can create 'micro-silos' that trigger rare device OOMs and expensive GPU driver recovery.

Short-term actions we pushed:
- Node isolation + rolling restarts (Monica)
- Temporary reduction of max-prefetch and reduced batch sizes for Veritas lane
- Added a kernel-level guard to catch imminent slab exhaustion and fall back to a smaller-kernel execution path before emitting a hard OOM

Medium-term (next 72 hours):
- Runtime patch to improve allocator defragmentation heuristics (backport to hosted fleet)
- Add a targeted metric and alert for device fragmentation ratio per pool
- Recommend Veritas pin their model to a slightly smaller KV window for the demo to avoid edge case trigger

I'll prepare a short exec-note for the board and a customer-facing comms template.

—Aditya
